_meta.what_this_is: A set of (x, y) points with a genuine linear relationship, and a restricted range of x. Measuring the correlation over the FULL range shows the relationship clearly. Measuring it over only a narrow slice of x -- what happens when you study only a pre-selected subgroup, like only admitted students or only top performers -- attenuates the correlation, because restricting the range shrinks the variation in x relative to the noise, and a real relationship looks weak or absent. The relationship did not change; the range you looked at did.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The points are hand-authored so the full-range correlation is strong (0.92) while the same points restricted to x in [5,8] give a weak correlation (0.31). Every correlation is computed in restriction.py.
_meta.format: points: [[x,y]]; restrict_lo, restrict_hi: the x-range the restricted view keeps.
